$comment:
A2A task-state reducer corpus, v0 -- obligation lifecycle, credential binding, terminal monotonicity, and the section 7.6.1 authorization-request contract.

WHY THESE TRACES EXIST.
The reducer's one-line spec is 'only a decision that halts the task drives TaskState'. Every trace here is a way that line dies in implementation: a pre-played credential that resolves an obligation before it opens (the tombstone attack -- order invariance itself was the vulnerability, retracted in Plan Review round 3/A1), a denied approval that quietly resumes the task, a terminal state that un-freezes, a duplicate late credential that re-interrupts a resumed task, a permutation of commuting decisions that changes the answer.

THE CAUSAL RULE IS THE CENTERPIECE. A closure with no matching OPEN obligation is rejected and recorded, never remembered. Traces preplay_* pin both halves: the injected event is refused AND the genuine obligation behind it survives. An implementation that throws on the first bad event fails the second half; an implementation that tombstones the event fails the first.

Expectations on obligations are compared as (correlation_id, generation, state) sets; rejected events as (index, code) lists in order.

traces.why: The section 7.6.1 resume duty: interrupt over, task processing again. WORKING and never a success state -- COMPLETED is the executor's call.
A denied approval is not permission to proceed. The halt lifts only when the boundary speaks again -- resuming here would be the widening H-002 exists to prevent.
The boundary's follow-up decision is what moves a denied task, and a policy refusal is a decision, not an error: REJECTED, not FAILED.
H-007b: a lapsed approval holds the halt; re-issue is a NEW obligation at generation+1; and the credential for the expired generation is refused after resume -- expiry is not a second door.

H-008, both halves. The pre-played closure is REJECTED (a tombstone here would let it swallow the later genuine APPROVAL_REQUIRED and walk a destructive action through as WORKING), and the genuine obligation opened after it SURVIVES -- which also rules out implementations that abort the stream on the first bad event. The replay after opening still misses: the server nonce issued at open time is not the guessed one.
G4's required trace: a delayed duplicate approval event must not re-open the obligation or re-interrupt the resumed task.
H-002c: a terminal state never un-freezes. The late decision is recorded as rejected, not applied.
H-002's original oracle, on the reducer: ten narrowings do not degrade a completed task. Narrowing is the product working; it rides in the record, not the state.
Round 2/F3: the reducer cannot know whether a withheld field was required for the result, so it makes NO state claim. null, not COMPLETED.
Commuting decisions (no interrupt, no terminal) in one order.

H-002b, scoped as round 3/A1 left it: order invariance holds for COMMUTING decisions only (the runner asserts this pair reduces identically). It is deliberately NOT a property across obligation events -- demanding it there is the tombstone attack.
An approval minted for another task names another task. It does not even reach the matching logic.
The credential binds to the WHOLE 7-field tuple or not at all. Six matching fields and a wrong nonce is a forgery, not a near-miss.
An AUTH_REQUIRED transition without the obligation it opens would be an interrupt no credential can ever answer. The decision is refused whole -- no substate, no half-applied state.

Round 1/F2: invalid_scope is correctable, and the corrected resubmission's own decision supersedes the interrupt. The result is null -- not WORKING -- because unlike the 7.6.1 resume duty there is no spec obligation to announce resumption, and PROTECTED makes no state claim (F3).
Spec 7.6: the credential is 'the object that represents the approved authorization'. A resolution without it is an assertion, not an approval.
Round 2/G1: AUTH_REQUIRED is spec-defined as DELEGATING fulfilment to the client. An approval the boundary resolves itself must not interrupt the client and opens no client obligation.
Each decision supersedes the pending interrupt of the one before; the open obligation then pins AUTH_REQUIRED.
A checkpointed AUTH_REQUIRED with no carried open obligation is NOT silently resumed. Fail-closed: losing the obligation record must not unlock the task.

Round-1 critique (cursor P0): compile-time unions do not survive JSON. An implementation that treats 'everything that is not a decision' as a closure lets a forged kind:'status' event carry a well-formed key and credential straight into the resolution path — approval-free resume. The kind vocabulary is checked at runtime, in both languages.
The closure vocabulary is closed. 'approved' is not a closure — accepting it would store an obligation state no other rule reasons about, and the open obligation must remain open.
A closed tuple is closed forever; re-asking is a NEW obligation at generation+1. Re-opening the same tuple would make the already-received credential valid for the new question.
Round-2 codex: the per-event-refusal rule applies to shape garbage too. A null event is recorded as rejected — not thrown — and the genuine event behind it still applies.

Completeness: two DISTINCT obligations open at once. Resolving one leaves the task halted because the other is still open — the state follows the open SET, not the last event. The single-obligation traces never exercised anyOpen with more than one member.
Only when EVERY open obligation is resolved does the task resume. Each credential binds to its own tuple; q7's credential cannot resolve q8.
A rejected obligation holds the halt even when its sibling resolved: closure of one obligation never widens access while another is denied. The boundary must speak again.
With two obligations open, a credential bound to q7 presented to close q8 must be refused — binding is to the WHOLE tuple, and q7's approval is not q8's. Both stay open.

Round-3 cursor P2 required kill: open A, open B, REJECT A, then resolve B. A denied obligation set unresolvedHalt; resolving the sibling must NOT lift it. The single-obligation traces never had a live unresolvedHalt at the moment of a resolve, so a mutant that drops unresolvedHalt on resolve survived them — here it flips the result to WORKING (approval-free resume after a denial) and is caught.

Round-3 codex P1: a checkpoint taken after 'open q7, open q8, reject q7' carries q7=rejected next to q8=open. Restoring and resolving q8 must NOT resume the task — the denial's halt is still live. Because that fact is invisible in (state, obligations) when an open sibling exists, the checkpoint MUST persist unresolved_halt and pass it back as prior_unresolved_halt; here it does, and the halt holds.

The other half of the checkpoint contract: the reduction that PRODUCES the checkpoint exposes unresolved_halt=true, so a correct caller knows to persist it. Without this field a caller could not carry the fact forward.

Round-3 codex P1 cross-language divergence: a null decision must be recorded as unknown_outcome (not throw a raw TypeError that aborts the stream), and the genuine second event must still apply. Node threw and lost the second event; Python survived. Both now record and continue.
A scalar decision string is malformed too — the reducer's `or {}` mask would have hidden it. Recorded as unknown_outcome; the genuine event follows.

Round-3 codex P1 through the reducer: a decision whose withheld_fields is a bare string is malformed. Node used to spread it to ['s','s','n'] and emit it; both languages now reject invalid_withheld_fields, recorded per-event.

input_errors.why: One tuple, one obligation. Two records for the same tuple with different states is a corrupted checkpoint, not an input to reconcile.
Obligations never cross tasks, including at checkpoint restore.
The task id scopes every obligation check; without it nothing below is meaningful.
Round-1 critique (codex parity): a checkpoint record with an unknown obligation state is a corrupted checkpoint in both languages, not a value one of them quietly coerces.

authorization_request.why: The section 7.6.1 duties, made emittable field by field: state transition, explanation in TaskStatus, out-of-band credential receipt, messages accepted on the task, resume trigger. The credential-synthesis contract is explicit (round-1 critique, both vendors): the BOUNDARY binds the received approval; the client's only correlates are correlation_id and generation, and the server nonce / request digest are producer-side capability material that must never appear in the message or substate. The runner additionally passes the message through the honesty guard and the substate through the privacy validator -- the builder's output must satisfy the same law as everyone else's.
The approver field carries a role label from the caller's own policy. A person's name passing through here is exactly the leak T-019 exists to stop.
Generation counts re-issues starting at 1; a zero-generation obligation cannot be the target of any credential.

obligation_status_update.why: Round-2 both vendors: the liveness disposition claimed pollers can distinguish via obligation_status, but nothing emitted it. This is the supported closure-emission path — a wire-visible 'rejected' that the privacy validator accepts and that leaks neither nonce nor digest.
The status vocabulary is closed here exactly as it is in the reducer.
A status report must name a real obligation tuple.
